evidence.note: Falsifiable claim: a claim whose declared globs overlap another live lease by prefix is GRANTED under [locks].acquire=lazy (globs advisory) but REFUSED under declared; the exact-file lease is taken at first write via lease.renewed held. Refuting observation: two items declared dir/** and dir/x.py, claimed lazy by two agents -> second claim exits 0; under declared -> exit 3. Cheapest test: tests/test_lease_lazy.py::test_lazy_claim_grants_prefix_overlap_and_records_mode (exit 0, lease.mode==lazy, held==[]) PASSES; test_declared_claim_still_refuses_prefix_overlap (exit 3) PASSES. Both run green on the branch. Design follows accepted D-lock-lifecycle-answers (lock-at-first-write enforced) and LK-hook-snapshot/LK-write-hook-wire for hook transport.

Rules read via ddflow brief and the item guidance budget: r-task-phase-needs-wave, r-small-files, r-lock-cycle-selfheal, r-gemini-key-load. Constraints honored: claim-is-not-process (D-dflow-claim-is-not-process), cli/mcp parity, help-first. GEMINI_API_KEY exported before any review.

Implemented on branch ddflow/DX-lease-lazy-acquire: [locks].acquire declared|lazy knob; lazy claim records advisory globs (mode=lazy) and skips prefix-overlap refusal; pre-edit hook acquires exact files via lease.renewed held; shared/new-file globs exempt; directory-over-hot-file claim warning. Commits 615bec2b2 1575c1f55 c23a1da41.

chunk_findings.detail: The new lease-snapshot validator only checks that `mode` is a string; it does not enforce the closed choice set introduced by `[locks].acquire` (`declared` or `lazy`). Given a lease snapshot containing `mode="lazyish"` (or `"lazy "`, `"Lazy"`, etc.), `_snapshot` returns `out["mode"] = "lazyish"` instead of raising `ValueError`, even though it rejects a non-string `mode` and negative TTL values. This lets an invalid lease mode persist and be consumed by the new lazy/declared logic; depending on the downstream check, a typo can silently fall back to declared locking or an unknown mode can be treated as lazy, defeating the knob’s declared choices.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/leasesnap.py:_snapshot

chunk_findings.detail: `acquire_files` grants an exact-file hold without checking that no other live lease already holds any requested file. It only validates `lease.holder == holder`; it never consults `state.live` or other items’ `lease.held`. Given two lazy claims `A` and `B` held by `alice` and `bob`, if `alice` has already acquired `foo.py` and `bob`’s first-write hook calls `acquire_files("B", "bob", ["foo.py"])`, the function appends `lease.renewed` with `foo.py` in `held` and returns success. Two live leases then hold the same exact file, defeating the “lock-at-first-write” enforcement and allowing simultaneous edits/lost updates.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leases/lifecycle.py:acquire_files

chunk_findings.detail: `acquire_files` ignores lease expiry/liveness. It reads `state.items.get(item_id).lease` directly and only compares holder, not `lease.expired(now)` or the fold’s `live` view. If a lazy lease’s TTL has passed (so `lease.expired(now)` is true and other lease code treats the files as free) but no `lease.expired`/release event has been folded yet, the same holder’s call to `acquire_files` succeeds and appends `lease.renewed` with `at=now`, silently resurrecting the expired lease. This violates the “released when merged or idle” rule and can let a stale holder continue writing after another agent has been allowed to take the file.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leases/lifecycle.py:acquire_files

chunk_findings.detail: The new lazy branch uses `cover = lz.get("held")` with no fallback. If a live lease entry has `mode: lazy` but no `held` key (or a malformed/missing `held` list from a partially upgraded snapshot or mode-only update), the generator `inside(rel, g) for g in cover` raises `TypeError`. That exception is swallowed by the broad `except Exception`, so `_holder` returns `""` for the whole call instead of merely ignoring the bad lease. Example: snapshot leases ordered as `{"1": {"holder": "B", "mode": "lazy", "renewed_at": now, "ttl_s": 60}, "2": {"holder": "C", "mode": "declared", "globs": ["a.py"], "renewed_at": now, "ttl_s": 60}}`; `_holder(repo, "A", "a.py")` should return `C`, but the missing `held` on lease 1 aborts the loop and returns `""`, letting A edit a file C leases.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/lanehooks_check.py:_holder

chunk_findings.detail: When a path is outside the lane worktree, `rel is None` and the code appends `"<raw> (outside the lane worktree)"` to `refuse`. Later it calls `_first_holder` with `[x for x in refuse if not x.endswith(")")]`, so outside-path entries are filtered out; if they are the only refusals, `holder` is false, yet the returned message still says `... is held by another lane...`. For example, in lazy mode a call with a single outside path such as `/tmp/foo.py` is refused with a lease-conflict reason even though the real reason is that the path is outside the worktree. The same suffix-based filter also drops any legitimate refused file path ending in `)` from the holder lookup, so the holder is not named even when `_holder` found one.
